title: Dynamic Overload via False Pivots
definition: A tactical system using advanced pivots as false 10s and a dropping center-back to create numerical superiority and connect defensive and attacking lines.
content: This concept describes a flexible attacking structure, often seen in 3-2-5 or 3-1-6 formations, designed to exploit opponent pressing or low blocks. The core mechanism involves advanced pivots acting as 'false 10s,' staying high to create a front-line overload, while a central defender drops deep to receive the ball. This movement attracts the opposition's press, freeing wide fullbacks to invert into central spaces for third-man passes. If the opponent defends deep, the team overloads the midfield vertically by having one pivot drop to a false 6 role, forcing the opponent to stretch vertically. This creates gaps behind their defensive line or allows the team to outnumber their box midfield. The system relies on dynamic positional interchanges: the middle center-back acts as a false pivot to connect lines, while the front five maintain horizontal width to pin backmarkers. This approach ensures numerical superiority in both the build-up and final third, allowing the team to switch play or penetrate central spaces based on the opponent's defensive reaction.
example_questions: How do we connect our defense to our attack without losing the ball?
Our center-backs are too far back and our midfield is too high, how do we bridge that gap?
What is the role of the dropping defender when we are trying to build from the back?
We struggle to find an extra man in midfield to play through, what tactical adjustment helps?
